top_story: A month into the US-Iran ceasefire, the truce is nearing collapse as fresh Iranian missile attacks and a costly stalemate sharpen pressure on both governments and revive the escalation logic Tehran articulated in March after threats against its power grid and the Strait of Hormuz. This renewed brinkmanship is not confined to military signaling; it is unfolding alongside acute domestic strain inside Iran, where imprisoned Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi is reportedly near death after suspected heart attacks under guard. Her condition underscores how the same security posture driving regional confrontation also continues to absorb dissent through coercion at home. The emerging picture is of an Iranian system responding to external pressure with both outward escalation and inward repression, increasing the risk that regional instability and domestic human costs will deepen together.
